scope: Compose accepted PacketChannel, ReserveAutonomousController and UseHistoryLedger so a real paid peer reply becomes actor-owned support evidence, influences the actor's route-free owned demand decision, and contributes to the selected paid movement and later paid consumer. This is the support-admission/settlement seam, not the complete parent social retention gate.

parent_split.FT7.1b1: Packet-mediated support admission, exact peer content contribution to actual chosen work and paid downstream use, load-v1 supported reserve accounting and success-v1 supported history classification
parent_split.FT7.1b2: Autonomous peer production/request coupling, subsequent independent training/closure and scoped retention under changed support, plus integrated tie-only feedback across later owned decisions
parent_split.common_gate: The unchanged FT7.1/FT7 requirement remains: same demand, packet, native processing and scoped capability rules within and between agents; actual contributions change later usable output; removing a contribution/uptake breaks the relevant claim. Neither supplied peer opportunities nor supported counters establish autonomous peer generation or independent capability.

implementation.policies: Use selected load-v1 reserve, initial 4 and declared load 1; successful supported settlement loses exactly one reserve unit. Use success-v1 history; only complete committed native paid-use deltas can be classified and supported work grants zero independent credit. No runtime default changes.
implementation.ownership: Native engine owns objects, payments, access, consent and all operation results. PacketChannel owns ordered intake; ReserveAutonomousController owns demand/request/route/consumer/settlement; UseHistoryLedger owns finite paid-use classification. New wrapper owns composition phase, exact baseline journal identity, one incoming peer-reply packet reference and causal links. It never writes native state or creates a certificate.
implementation.order: Queue at most one realized peer reply through the unchanged authorized PacketChannel. Each nonterminal wrapper step first advances channel delivery with declared participant availability. While that packet is partial or waiting, no native route is launched. Once uptake completes, or if no packet exists, invoke the accepted autonomous reserve controller. It forms the request from the actor's current paid owned need and discovers support only in its owned view. Continue actual paid comparison, chosen movement and paid consumer to the accepted settlement condition.
implementation.history: At terminal cycle boundary, classify exact post-baseline native paid-use deltas once: actual supported traversal plus successful consumer means supported; actual independent traversal plus successful consumer means independent; unsuccessful terminal attempt means failed. Zero-delta histories receive empty classifications. A waiting/partial run has only the unchanged baseline ledger, not fabricated completion credit. No per-turn decay claim or new feedback-choice claim is made here; live tie integration remains FT7.1b2.
implementation.checkpoint: Exact paired native hash, actor, baseline count/hash, packet key, channel, reserve cycle, history and indexed wrapper events. Restore must preserve partial native uptake or work and all nested checkpoint identities. No external success, route, recipe, output answer, certificate or desired final seat enters step.

fixed_panel.support_allowed: The existing native peer identity only; relation labels confer no skill or permission.
fixed_panel.construction: Use the accepted native fixture primitives without deleting access: construct a same-scope source model, a two-participant group, actual paid sender offer and actual paid peer reply, and expose the offer to its lawful audience. Do not expose/read the final peer reply for the receiver. Bind a native actor-owned need after these opportunities are prepared. Canonical need weights favor shared output; workflow need priorities favor shared output. Peer consent is a typed content operand, changed at constant labels and native request form. The receiver's native selector, never the fixture, chooses its eventual recipe and work.
fixed_panel.controls: Nonconsent changes only the peer's typed consent operand. No-packet retains the same unreceived reply and starts the owned decision without queuing it. Withdrawn leaves the emitted packet pending because the receiver is unavailable. Partial-uptake advances only one paid read unit, then withholds receiver availability through the horizon; no retained content or route is permitted. Preserve unavailable/deferred/unsupported results.
fixed_panel.restart: In both settings, split one consented run after its first partial uptake step and finish both branches with the same availability/quanta. Native and wrapper checkpoints must be byte-exact. Two additional restart records; primary panel remains ten scenarios.
fixed_panel.matching: Same actor TIM, native scope, owned demand, offered model, native group, initial wallets, load/reserve policy and four-facet requirement across each setting's matched cases. Nonconsent sender main operation costs must equal consented sender main costs. Packet removal or availability controls may legitimately remove receiver uptake cost; never call those controls equal-total-cost or successful.

gate: Sixteen exact methods pass with zero failures/errors, ten fixed scenarios plus two restart records preserve all identities and controls, both actual consented native runs choose lawful support and consume its exact peer-reply operand in paid chosen work followed by paid same-scope use, missing uptake/consent breaks that claim without granting independent credit, independent raw auditors reconstruct packet authority, owned demand, native choice, payments, content operands, reserve and history, all 281 predecessor methods remain exact and frozen source is unchanged. Passing accepts only FT7.1b1; parent FT7.1b/FT7.1 and FT7 remain pending FT7.1b2 and their common gates.
invariants: Preserve baseline, TIM, dimensionality, semantic scope versus physical target, grade-v1/legacy-r4 law/defaults, load-v1/success-v1 definitions, all prior failures, no fabricated peer authority, no supported certificate, no H.retained deletion or subtype/C/D election. Auditors import no audited wrapper, executor, chooser or scheduler. Native record getters may be supplied to the unchanged accepted independent reserve auditor.
next: FT7.1b2 prospective autonomous peer production and scoped independent later reuse; retain all FT7 ordered-pair/population and FT8/FT9 gates.
